requirements.title: RETURN and END do not undefine nonpointer blank-common data
requirements.definition: Executing RETURN or END does not cause nonpointer data objects in blank common to become undefined. The named-common comparison remains conditional under19.6.6 and SAVE, and pointer association status and target lifetime are separate. This guarantee does not initialize previously undefined objects.

requirements.title: Named common of one name has one complete size across a program
requirements.definition: Every scoping unit in a program that declares the same named common block gives it the same complete storage-sequence size, including equivalence extensions. Blank common may have different sizes, but matching-prefix and associated-type restrictions still apply.

requirements.title: Blank-common objects are not initially defined
requirements.definition: Blank-common objects cannot be initially defined. The neighboring permission allows named-common initialization by DATA or a type declaration in BLOCK DATA under the canonical initialization and complete-block rules; it does not provide a new local initialization effect.

RETURN/END retention is for nonpointer blank COMMON; named-common undefinition is conditional and SAVE never initializes data or extends dead targets. Named size equality includes every declaring scope and equivalence extension; blank unequal sizes retain identical prefixes. Named BLOCK DATA initialization permission preserves C808/C880, complete block specification, one BLOCK DATA declaration and storage-unit uniqueness; blank initial definition remains prohibited.
